q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is 2026-08-24. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release is August 26, 2026 (in 2 days). This question asks for **forward guidance** issued at that earnings release, not actual Q2 results. The guidance will typically be for Q3 FY2027 revenue.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks about NVIDIA's **forward guidance** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. Based on the research:
- NVIDIA just issued Q2 guidance in May of $91.0B ± 2% (range: $89.2B-$92.8B)
- Q1 FY2027 actual came in at $81.6B, beating $78.0B guidance
- Analysts anticipate Q3 guidance around $107-$108B based on Street Signal
- There's a consistent pattern of NVIDIA exceeding guidance and demonstrating strong demand momentum

For the forward guidance (which would be for Q3), I'd expect NVIDIA to:
1. Maintain its established ±2% guidance margin (their typical practice)
2. Guide higher than Q2 given momentum and demand strength
3. The Street Signal article specifically mentions "Q3 guide around $107-$108 billion"

The most likely guidance midpoint appears to be in the **$105-$108B range**, which aligns with analyst expectations cited in the research.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Significant geopolitical complications (China export restrictions tightening)
- Unexpected macro slowdown or customer capex delays
- Manufacturing/supply chain disruptions
- Competitive pressures materializing faster than expected
- NVIDIA becoming more conservative after a beat (though unlikely given their track record)
- Broader AI capex budget constraints emerging

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued momentum from Q1 beat ($81.6B vs $78.0B guidance)
- Stronger-than-expected enterprise AI demand
- New product cycles or customer wins announced
- Continued beat-and-raise pattern (NVIDIA has shown this tendency)
- H100/H200 ramp accelerating
- The $107-$108B analyst expectations turning out conservative

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027: Actual $81.6B vs. Guided $78.0B ± 2% (beat by ~$2.6B or 3.3%)
- Q2 FY2027: Guided $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B-$92.8B floor/ceiling)
- Q3 FY2027 analyst expectations: "around $107-$108 billion" per Street Signal

NVIDIA's pattern shows they typically guide conservatively and beat, then provide modestly higher guidance for the following quarter. The beat in Q1 ($81.6B vs $78.0B) suggests strong underlying demand.

## Analysis of the range

The question range is $99.5B-$115.5B (open on both ends). The analyst expectations of $107-$108B fall squarely in this range and represent the most credible forward-looking estimates we have.

Given:
- Analyst consensus: $107-$108B
- NVIDIA's typical ±2% guidance bands
- Strong momentum from Q1 beat
- The midpoint of analyst expectations: ~$107.5B

I estimate the forward guidance will likely be around $105-$110B, with the most probable central estimate around $107B.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings report on Wednesday, August 26, after the close of trading [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued in May, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is slightly higher at approximately $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance of $78.0 billion (plus or minus 2%) by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Some analysts are now anticipating Q2 revenue to be in the $94-$95 billion range, with a Q3 guide around $107-$108 billion [streetsignal.substack.com](https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/nvda-earnings-bridge).
